changes.value: Strongest feature: White precisely distinguishes the continuing relevance of good news from any necessity for altering Gospel narratives, directly challenging Crossan's updating definition and justifying precisionClarity 82, responsiveness 78, logicalCoherence 75, and relevanceBurden 76. Principal limitation: His excerpt asserts New Testament usage and timeless efficacy without textual examples, proves only that alteration is unnecessary rather than absent, and compresses Crossan's literary evidence into a presuppositional definition, fitting evidenceWarrant 61 and calibrationCharity 69. Live burden: White must examine particular inter-Gospel changes and demonstrate that unchanged historical content explains their community-specific forms better than Crossan's contextual-redaction account. Locked score: The immutable 73 accurately registers a central, clearly framed objection with substantial burden contact, while withholding stronger credit because possibility of faithful transmission cannot establish nonalteration or answer affirmative evidence of revision.

Strongest feature: Crossan directly answers White by presenting Gospel transmission as a stream in which Mark may rephrase Jesus for a later community while preserving spiritual authenticity, supporting responsiveness 81, relevanceBurden 81, precisionClarity 77, and logicalCoherence 73. Principal limitation: The imagined scenario of Mark possessing recordings supplies no canonical example of invention, while four versions alone cannot establish that community need licenses fabrication or define how authenticity survives it, appropriately fixing evidenceWarrant 60 and calibrationCharity 69. Live burden: Crossan must identify concrete reformulations, distinguish invention from selection or paraphrase, and provide a principled criterion showing when altered narrative remains authentically Jesus's message. Locked score: The immutable 73 reflects a central and responsive contextual-redaction model whose evidential demonstration and standard of spiritual sameness remain insufficient for the stronger historical conclusion.
